title: Whole-mount immunofluorescence staining of mesenchymal progenitors in murine plantaris muscle
protocol: Sacrifice the mouse.
Peel off the skin to expose the lower leg muscles.
Cut the Achilles tendon of the gastrocnemius and soleus muscles while leaving the plantaris muscle intact.
Pinch the Achilles tendon of the gastrocnemius and soleus muscles by forceps and pull them away from the tibia to expose the plantaris muscle.
Cut the Achilles tendon of the plantaris muscle.
Pinch the Achilles tendon of the plantaris muscle by forceps and pull it away from the tibia.
Cut the proximal attachment site of the plantaris muscle to the femur and isolate the whole muscle.
Pour 4% PFA solution onto a silicone rubber plate and keep it on ice.
Immerse the plantaris muscle in the 4% PFA solution.
Pin both ends of the plantaris muscle using intradermal needles as quickly as possible.
Fix the muscle for 30 minutes on ice.
Transfer the fixed muscle to a 2.0 mL tube containing PBS.
Wash the muscle with PBS three times, each wash lasting 30 minutes.
Remove PBS from the tube.
Add blocking solution to the tube.
Incubate the muscle in blocking solution at 4°C for 12 h.
Remove blocking solution from the tube.
Add goat polyclonal anti-mouse PDGFRα (final concentration: 2.5 μg/mL) and rabbit monoclonal anti-YAP (dilution: 1:100) diluted in blocking solution containing 1% Triton X-100 to the tube.
Incubate the muscle at 4°C for 12 hours.
Wash the muscle with PBS for 30 minutes three times.
Remove PBS from the tube.
Add Alexa 647-conjugated donkey anti-goat IgG and Alexa 594-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG diluted in blocking solution (dilution: 1:1000) to the tube.
Incubate the muscle at 4°C for 12 hours in the dark.
Remove secondary antibodies from the tube.
Add DAPI diluted in blocking solution (dilution: 1:5000) to the tube.
Incubate the muscle at 4°C for 10 minutes in the dark.
Wash the muscle with PBS for 30 minutes three times.
Use enough volume (e.g., 500–600 μL) of secondary antibody and DAPI solution to completely soak the muscle.
Protect the sample from light after secondary antibody staining.
Store the stained muscle in PBS for up to 1 week at 4°C, protecting from light.
Place the silicone rubber sheet on a cover glass.
Put a few drops of mounting medium on the muscle placed on the cover glass framed by silicone rubber sheet.
Cover the sample with another cover glass to sandwich it between two cover glasses.
Store the mounted specimen at 4°C, protected from light, for up to 2 weeks.
Obtain z-stack images of the immunofluorescently stained whole muscle using a confocal laser scanning microscope.
Follow the manufacturer’s instructions for detailed settings of each microscope.
Adjust the laser power and detector gain to obtain appropriate signal in each channel while using a negative control sample for background settings.
Set the start and end positions for z-stack imaging.
Determine the scan interval in the z-axis direction considering the optical resolution of the objective lens.
Use an objective lens with adequate working distance to cover the depth of the sample for whole-mount observation.
Set the laser intensity to a sufficient level at the deepest part of the sample for z-stack images.
Move the focus to the surface of the sample and check that the signal is not saturated at all depths.
Use the microscope's function to set the laser intensity in steps according to the sample depth if available.
Test the degree of fading of the fluorescent dyes in the sample using a test sample.
Set the end position for z-stack imaging at a depth of less than 50 μm from the muscle surface.
Acquire the z-stack images.
Reconstruct the maximum intensity projection image using appropriate 3D imaging software.
